artists.biography: Death in Vegas are a psychedelic rock and electronic rock band from the United Kingdom, comprising two permanent members: Richard Fearless (Richard Maguire) and Tim Holmes. Influenced by a wide range of musical genres including psychedelic rock, electronica, krautrock, dub and industrial, the band's sound is constantly changing, moving between live rock sounds, electronica and minimal techno. The band was formed in 1994 by Fearless and Steve Hellier and signed to Concrete Records under the name of "Dead Elvis". Objections from the Elvis Presley estate forced them to change their name, and Dead Elvis became the title of their first album instead.

perplexity.description:
Scorpio Rising is the third studio album by British electronic band Death in Vegas, originally released in 2002 on Concrete Records. The album blends electronic music with elements of rock, trip hop, and neo-psychedelia, creating a dark, atmospheric sound that marked a significant evolution in the band’s style. Recorded at their own Contino Rooms studio in London, the album features lush string arrangements by L. Subramaniam and guest vocals from notable artists including Liam Gallagher, Hope Sandoval, Nicola Kuperus, and Paul Weller, adding depth and variety to its sonic palette.

Within Death in Vegas’ discography, Scorpio Rising stands as a pivotal release, bridging their earlier, more abrasive electronic work with a more refined, genre-blurring approach. The album’s title references Kenneth Anger’s experimental film, reflecting its cinematic and moody aesthetic. Upon release, Scorpio Rising received positive critical attention for its ambitious production and eclectic collaborations, though it did not achieve major commercial success. It remains a respected entry in the band’s catalog and a notable example of early 2000s British electronic rock.
